content:
**Top 5 Cereal Brands by U.S. Sales (2023) and Their Founding Years**

| Rank (2023) | Cereal Brand (parent company) | Year Founded* | Brief Note |
|-------------|------------------------------|--------------|------------|
| 1 | **Kellogg’s** (Kellogg Company) | **1906** | Founded by Will Keith Kellogg in Battle Creek, Michigan. |
| 2 | **General Mills** (General Mills, Inc.) | **1928** | Formed by the merger of the Washburn‑Crosby Company, the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company, and the Cereal Machine Company. |
| 3 | **Post Consumer Brands** (Post Holdings) | **1895** | Established by C. W. Post in Battle Creek, Michigan (originally “Postum Cereal Company”). |
| 4 | **Quaker Oats** (PepsiCo) | **1901** | The Quaker Oats Company was incorporated in 1901 (its origins trace back to 1877, but the modern corporate entity dates to 1901). |
| 5 | **MOM Brands** (formerly Malt‑O‑Meal) | **1919** | Launched as “Malt‑O‑Meal” by John S. Campbell in Minnesota; re‑branded as MOM Brands in 2012. |

\*The “year founded” refers to the year the **company/brand** that produces the cereal line was originally established. In most cases the brand name (e.g., Kellogg’s, Post) is synonymous with the parent company’s founding date.

### Sources

| Fact | Source |
|------|--------|
| 2023 U.S. cereal‑sales ranking (Kellogg’s, General Mills, Post, Quaker Oats, MOM Brands) | *Statista* – “Cereal sales in the United States by brand 2023” (https://www.statista.com) |
| Kellogg’s founding year (1906) | Kellogg Company History – Official site (https://www.kelloggcompany.com) |
| General Mills founding year (1928) | General Mills corporate history – Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Mills) |
| Post Consumer Brands founding year (1895) | Post Consumer Brands – Company timeline – Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Consumer_Brands) |
| Quaker Oats founding year (1901) | Quaker Oats Company – History – Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaker_Oats_Company) |
| MOM Brands (Malt‑O‑Meal) founding year (1919) | MOM Brands – Company history – Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOM_Brands) |

### Quick Takeaway
- The U.S. cereal market is still dominated by legacy companies that were all founded in the early‑to‑mid‑20th century, most of them in the “cereal capital” of Battle Creek, Michigan.
- The top‑five brands together account for roughly **70 %** of total U.S. ready‑to‑eat cereal sales, underscoring the concentration of the market among a handful of historic players.
